section_summary: This section closes a 1936 Navy report alleging espionage and other unlawful activity by Japanese naval vessels and residents in Hawaii, then documents the 1937 interdepartmental effort to formulate a federal response. The papers review suspicious tanker visits, possible clandestine landing of naval personnel, military photography, propaganda, and the use of Japanese-operated fishing vessels for observation or covert movement. Proposed remedies included surveillance at Honolulu, restrictions on visits to other Hawaiian ports, stricter customs and immigration enforcement, identification of fishing crews, diplomatic representations to Japan, and new federal and territorial legislation.

subfiles.title: Concluding findings on Japanese naval and civilian activities in Hawaii
subfiles.to: Secretary of the Navy and other federal officials
subfiles.about: Concludes that Japanese ship visits and associated local activity may violate espionage, customs, and territorial laws and recommends investigation and executive action.
subfiles.summary: Concluding findings: the Tsurumi's Midway reconnaissance and the Ondo crew's photography and customs violations at Hilo and Waimea were inimical to defense; recommends State investigation and presidential direction; Swanson approved September 18, 1936.

subfiles.title: Department of State routing note on confidential material
subfiles.from: Department of State, Office of Coordination and Review
subfiles.about: Records confidential handling and contemplated hand delivery of material to the War Department.
subfiles.summary: Routing note: an item placed under double cover for the War Department, to be hand-delivered next morning.

subfiles.title: Designation of Stanley K. Hornbeck for preliminary discussions
subfiles.about: Names Stanley K. Hornbeck as the State Department representative in preliminary discussions of Japanese activities in Hawaii.
subfiles.summary: Hull designates Stanley Hornbeck for preliminary discussions on objectionable activities by Japanese in Hawaii.

subfiles.title: Letter transmitting California Joint Immigration Committee Document No. 501
subfiles.from: California Joint Immigration Committee; V. S. McClatchy
subfiles.about: Supplies a document omitted from a footnote in the committee's June 18 statement.
subfiles.summary: California Joint Immigration Committee sends Hull Document No. 501 on alleged Japanese propaganda in public schools.

subfiles.title: More Japanese Propaganda in the Public Schools
subfiles.about: Accuses the American Council of the Institute of Pacific Relations and associated textbook writers of presenting misleading pro-Japanese material in schools.
subfiles.summary: Memo reviews disputed textbooks in Hawaiian and California schools and singles out Helen Pratt's 'Japan, Where Ancient Loyalties Survive' for obscuring facts on the Gentlemen's Agreement and exclusion.

subfiles.title: Internal note requesting Wilson's attendance
subfiles.about: Reports that the Secretary wants Hugh R. Wilson to attend the committee meeting and receive background on the case.
subfiles.summary: Note: Mr. Renchard called; the Secretary instructs Wilson to attend the meeting and asks Hamilton to brief him.

subfiles.title: State Department concerns about proposed fisheries legislation
subfiles.about: Explains two provisions in the draft committee report and cautions against legislation that would broadly eliminate alien ownership of fishing vessels.
subfiles.summary: State's concerns on fisheries bills: fingerprinting alien fishermen, and amending R.S. 4311 to eventually require citizen-owned fishing vessels. Espionage abuses can be controlled without risking treaty violations or retaliation.

subfiles.title: Invitation to consider the Working Committee report
subfiles.about: Invites the Secretary of State to a November 17 meeting of the Interdepartmental Committee to consider the Working Committee's completed report.
subfiles.summary: Woodring says the Working Committee finished its work, encloses its report and a proposed letter to the President, and proposes a meeting.

subfiles.title: Memorandum for the Secretary of War on Japanese activities in Hawaii
subfiles.about: Summarizes the committee's origin, membership, assigned problem, and principal concerns before transmitting recommendations.
subfiles.summary: Krueger recounts the October 1936 warning, the May 1937 committee, and practices under review: clandestine landings, unauthorized service members, suspicious craft, photography and observation equipment.

subfiles.title: Draft letter to the President recommending measures against Japanese activities in Hawaii
subfiles.from: Secretary of War as chairman of the Interdepartmental Committee
subfiles.about: Recommends administrative controls and legislation to counter suspected Japanese espionage and covert activity in Hawaii.
subfiles.summary: Draft letter recommends limiting Japanese public vessels to Honolulu, covert counts, customs observation, regulating alien fishing boats, representations to Japan, priority for S. 1485 and amending R.S. 4311.

subfiles.title: Designation of Wilson and Hamilton for the November 17 meeting
subfiles.about: Acknowledges the committee meeting and designates Hugh R. Wilson and Maxwell M. Hamilton to represent the State Department.
subfiles.summary: Hull appoints Assistant Secretary Wilson, with Hamilton, to the November 17 meeting on the Working Committee report.

subfiles.title: Record of the November 17 Interdepartmental Committee meeting
subfiles.to: Division of Far Eastern Affairs files
subfiles.about: Records approval of the draft presidential letter with a State Department qualification concerning foreign relations.
subfiles.summary: November 17 meeting approved the draft letter to the President, adding 'having due regard for our foreign relations' at State's proposal.

subfiles.title: Attendance list for the November 17 Interdepartmental Committee meeting
subfiles.about: Lists the departmental representatives expected at the meeting on Japanese naval and civil personnel in Hawaii.
subfiles.summary: Attendance list for the November 17 meeting: Wilson and Hamilton for State, others for Treasury, Navy, Interior and Labor; the Attorney General assented by letter.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference to Guy M. Gillette letter on Japanese consular activities
subfiles.about: Directs researchers to a Gillette letter concerning alleged Japanese consular organization of Asian residents against Caucasian citizens in Hawaii.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Guy Gillette's November 26, 1937 letter on statehood-commission evidence of improper Japanese consular activity in Hawaii.

subfiles.title: Notification of presidential approval of the committee report
subfiles.about: Reports that the President approved the committee report and ordered its recommendations implemented quickly.
subfiles.summary: Woodring says the President fully approved the November 17 report and directed putting recommendations into effect, with confidential letters to congressional chairmen.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of presidential approval
subfiles.about: Acknowledges notice that the President approved the committee report and requested prompt implementation and congressional action.
subfiles.summary: Hull records Woodring's notice of presidential approval and his letters to congressional chairmen on legislation.

subfiles.title: Supplementary Report: Activities of Japanese Naval and Civil Personnel in Hawaii
subfiles.from: Assistant Chief of Staff, G-2, and Director of Naval Intelligence
subfiles.about: Presents additional naval intelligence about suspicious Japanese tanker visits to Honolulu and an incident involving a U.S. sailor.
subfiles.summary: Supplementary report alleges visiting Japanese ships maintained contacts, spread propaganda, carried unlisted persons and left men in Honolulu, creating a communication channel; sailor Carroll was removed after photographing the Consul-General.

subfiles.title: War and Navy concerns requiring action in Hawaii
subfiles.about: Defines the Japanese naval and civilian practices that the War and Navy Departments particularly wanted terminated.
subfiles.summary: Krueger lists War and Navy concerns: suspected landings, unauthorized Japanese service members, suspicious craft, photography of Pearl Harbor and special cameras and range finders, including incidents at Hilo.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of Irving F. Wixon's immigration memorandum
subfiles.about: Forwards Wixon's secret analysis of immigration issues affecting Japanese naval and civilian personnel in Hawaii.
subfiles.summary: Krueger circulates Labor representative Irving Wixon's immigration memorandum for the Working Committee.

subfiles.title: Immigration and Naturalization Service analysis of Japanese personnel and fishing vessels
subfiles.about: Explains legal and practical obstacles to identifying and deporting Japanese personnel and checking crews of Hawaiian fishing vessels.
subfiles.summary: Wixon reports Coast Guard inspections of Japanese sampans and urges photographic, fingerprinted crew identification; deportation cases have evidentiary problems, and examining Japanese naval vessels could embarrass diplomacy.

subfiles.title: Call for another Working Committee meeting
subfiles.about: Proposes a September 21 meeting to formulate constructive recommendations on Japanese activities in Hawaii.
subfiles.summary: Krueger suggests the Working Committee reconvene at the Winder Building to prepare recommendations for the full Interdepartmental Committee.

subfiles.title: Hornbeck response to the proposed September 21 meeting
subfiles.about: Confirms that Hornbeck has reserved the proposed meeting date and will attend or send a substitute.
subfiles.summary: Hornbeck notes Krueger's proposed September 21 Working Committee meeting and will attend himself or send a substitute.

subfiles.title: Foreign public vessel notices and possible misinterpretation
subfiles.about: Questions whether standard courtesy notices for foreign public vessels might be misread as granting customs or immigration immunity.
subfiles.summary: Mrs. Buford says foreign public vessel notices only inform other departments and do not exempt personnel from customs or immigration rules; clearer wording is suggested.

subfiles.title: Handwritten note concerning checks of foreign public vessels
subfiles.about: Contains fragmentary comments concerning whether Labor or Customs authorities should check a foreign vessel and refers to an attachment.
subfiles.summary: Handwritten note, largely illegible, apparently on checking a vessel through Labor or Customs.

subfiles.title: Standard Department of State request for courtesies to a public vessel
subfiles.about: Provides standard language requesting the usual courtesies and facilities when no objection is perceived.
subfiles.summary: Blank State Department form requesting customary courtesies for a public vessel, the specimen wording discussed.

subfiles.title: Hamilton review of subcommittee recommendations
subfiles.about: Seeks approval to accept Ingersoll's draft recommendations for presentation to the full committee.
subfiles.summary: Hamilton finds Ingersoll's recommendations generally satisfactory but flags the new proposal to bar Japanese public vessels from Hawaiian ports other than Honolulu; he recommends no objection yet.

subfiles.title: State Department note on reciprocal restrictions on naval port visits
subfiles.about: Considers the legal and diplomatic implications of excluding Japanese vessels from Hawaiian ports.
subfiles.summary: Memo sees no reason to distinguish Japan's refusal of American visits to mandated-island ports from a US right to refuse Japanese visits to Hawaii, but questions whether retaliation is timely.

subfiles.title: Ingersoll letter transmitting draft subcommittee recommendations
subfiles.about: Forwards suggested recommendations on the matters referred to the Hawaii subcommittee.
subfiles.summary: Ingersoll sends Hamilton a draft of subcommittee recommendations, with a copy to Wixon.

subfiles.title: Recommendations for surveillance of Japanese naval vessels
subfiles.from: Subcommittee of Ingersoll, Hamilton, and Wixon
subfiles.about: Proposes covert counts, customs surveillance, diplomatic reporting, and limits on Japanese public-vessel visits in Hawaii.
subfiles.summary: Recommendations: covert counts of persons leaving and boarding Japanese vessels at Honolulu, reports of discrepancies to State, denial of other Hawaiian ports, and customs observation.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of proposed Working Committee report
subfiles.about: Circulates a proposed report and calls a November 5 meeting to consider it.
subfiles.summary: Krueger submits a draft Working Committee report and proposes meeting at the Winder Building November 5.

subfiles.title: Draft Working Committee report for the Secretary of War
subfiles.about: Sets out the committee's mandate, membership, concerns, and submission of a draft presidential letter.
subfiles.summary: Draft Working Committee report: formation of the committee, five principal concerns (landed personnel, unauthorized service members, suspicious craft, photography, observation equipment) and a draft letter to the President.

subfiles.title: Golden W. Bell's proposed revisions to the committee report
subfiles.about: Suggests revisions referring to accompanying legislative materials and describing the proposed measures as supplements to existing controls.
subfiles.summary: Golden Bell proposes the report transmit copies of congressional bills and Hawaiian legislation, state they supplement existing measures, and have Interior sponsor a Hawaiian bill like S. 1485.

subfiles.title: Revised draft letter to the President on Japanese activities in Hawaii
subfiles.from: Secretary of War as chairman of the Interdepartmental Committee
subfiles.about: Presents the committee's revised administrative and legislative recommendations.
subfiles.summary: Revised draft letter to the President: limit Japanese public vessels to Honolulu, covert checks, regulate alien-operated fishing boats, make representations to Japan, and prioritize S. 1485 and the R.S. 4311 amendment.

subfiles.title: Earlier draft memorandum for the Secretary of War
subfiles.about: Provides another draft account of the committee's creation, membership, concerns, and recommendation process.
subfiles.summary: Earlier draft memo repeating the October 1936 warning and May 1937 committee history and listing practices to stop in Hawaii.

subfiles.title: Earlier draft letter to the President
subfiles.from: Secretary of War as chairman of the Interdepartmental Committee
subfiles.about: Recommends port, surveillance, customs, diplomatic, and legislative measures, with a notation that part had not yet received State Department approval.
subfiles.summary: Earlier draft letter to the President on excluding Japanese public vessels from ports other than Honolulu, with a marginal note that State had not yet approved the vessel-ownership provision.

subfiles.title: Cover sheet for papers supplied by Captain Munter
subfiles.about: Identifies the following material as a copy of papers furnished by Captain Munter.
subfiles.summary: Cover sheet attributing papers to Captain Munter, for the Coast Guard representative.

subfiles.title: Excerpt from Commander Towle's letter on Japanese fishing vessels
subfiles.about: Reports discussions with Mr. Bland and military officers about controlling Japanese-owned fishing vessels and crews in Hawaii.
subfiles.summary: Towle describes Hawaii's fishing industry as largely controlled by Japanese owners and crews and recounts a conference with Bland, Naval Intelligence, Navy, and Army officers about proposed federal legislation. He argues that alien-owned small craft concentrated at Hawaii, San Pedro, and San Diego pose a strategic danger and urges identification papers, Coast Guard enforcement authority, and controls on vessel ownership and operation. He also proposes amendments to Hawaiian statutes governing fishermen's tags, vessel-registration data, citizenship declarations, and penalties, while noting political resistance to broad alien-registration measures.

subfiles.title: Commander Towle's proposed amendment to the federal vessel-numbering law
subfiles.to: U.S. Coast Guard and congressional reviewers
subfiles.about: Would impose citizenship, ownership, identification, permitting, and national-defense conditions on numbered vessels.
subfiles.summary: Commander Towle's proposed amendment to the vessel-numbering law: owner's oath of no foreign interest, alien identification certificates, citizen English-speaking operators and permits, with fines and forfeiture.

subfiles.title: Proposed amendment to Revised Statutes section 4311
subfiles.to: W. Y. Towle; information copy for R. R. Waesche
subfiles.about: Proposes restricting the coasting trade and fisheries to licensed American vessels while allowing a temporary exception for certain resident-alien owners.
subfiles.summary: Proposed amendment to Revised Statutes section 4311 defining vessels allowed in the coasting trade or fisheries, forfeiture for others, and a six-year transition for resident alien owners; for Admiral Waesche's information.

subfiles.title: S. 1485: Bill to prohibit photographs, sketches, or maps of vital defense installations
subfiles.from: David I. Walsh and Morris Sheppard
subfiles.to: United States Senate Committee on Naval Affairs
subfiles.about: Would criminalize unauthorized recording and dissemination of designated military and naval installations and equipment.
subfiles.summary: S. 1485 would authorize the President to designate vital installations, requiring permission and censorship for photographs, sketches and maps, with penalties up to $1,000, one year, or both.
